title: tc-claim-answer
description:
An AI answer marked up claim by claim: source type, confidence, uncertainty, the passages behind each claim and a
counter-position; claims can be sent to verification.

claims.description: The answer as claims, in order – each with its source type, confidence and sources; items without `source` are plain text

sources.description: The passages the claims rest on, looked up by id

counter.description: The strongest case against the answer – shown folded under it; empty hides it

open.description: Id of the claim whose detail is open (null: none)

queued.description: Ids of the claims already sent to verification – their button says so

now.description: The moment source freshness is counted to (epoch ms), passed to every validity badge; unset, each badge uses when it connected

confidenceBands.description: Confidence at or above `high` reads High, at or above `medium` Medium, else Low

sourceLabels.description: The names of the source types – your own vocabulary in place of Sourced, Model knowledge and Inferred

sourceNotes.description: What each source type means, in the open claim

uncertaintyLabels.description: The names of the uncertainty kinds – in place of Not settled, Thin evidence and Beyond the model

uncertaintyNotes.description: What each uncertainty kind means, in the open claim (a claim's own `note` follows it)

confidenceLabels.description: The words for the confidence levels – in place of High, Medium and Low

confidenceCeilings.description: The highest confidence shown for each source type, 0–1 – a transcript claim might go no higher than 0.7, whatever the model says. Unset types aren't capped

questionType.description: The kind of question the answer replies to, shown as a tag in the head; unset shows none

questionTypeLabels.description: The names of the question types – in place of Factual, Analytical, Predictive and Opinion

questionTypeNotes.description: What each question type means for the answer, in the tag's tooltip and for screen readers

verifyLabel.description: The button that sends a claim to verification

queuedLabel.description: What that button says once the claim is queued

text.description: The claim's words. Spaces at the start or end are kept outside the mark

source.description: Where it came from; leave it out for connecting text that claims nothing

confidence.description: How sure the model is, 0–1 – shown no higher than the type's ceiling and the `recognition`

recognition.description: Media types: how well the medium was read, 0–1 – OCR or speech-recognition confidence, shown beside the type ("OCR 87%"); the claim's confidence is shown no higher

uncertainty.description: Why it can't be certain, when that applies

note.description: A sentence on the uncertainty or the inference, e.g. "Only two studies, both small"

sources.description: Ids of the sources it rests on

AnswerClaim.description: One claim of the answer – or, without `source`, plain text between claims

ClaimSourceType.description: Where a claim came from: a retrieved source, the model's own knowledge, an inference from other claims – or a medium, or memory

ClaimMediaType.description: Read from a medium rather than a text: a machine transcript, a video, a recording, an image, or text read off a scan (OCR)

ClaimMemoryType.description: Remembered rather than retrieved now: an earlier session, the team's shared knowledge, or another agent's finding

ClaimUncertainty.description: Why a claim can't be certain: the world hasn't decided · the evidence is thin · it's beyond what the model can know

title.description: Headline of the page or document

quote.description: The passage the claim relies on

validity.description: How fresh the source is – shown as a tc-validity-badge

ClaimSource.description: A passage a claim rests on

observed.description: When the evidence was observed or published

band.description: The band, set outright – `observed` and the profile are then ignored

changed.description: The source has changed since it was used – the app compares what was relied on with what is there now

label.description: Strip: what the paragraph is called in its tooltip and to screen readers (default "Paragraph 2")

ValidityInfo.description: What a piece of evidence says about its freshness – one paragraph of a strip, or a source in tc-claim-answer

ValidityTime.description: A moment: epoch ms, an ISO date string or a Date

ValidityProfileName.description: Built-in decay profiles – fast: hours and days (prices, status, news) · standard: weeks and months · slow: years (reference material) · lasting: never decays

ValidityProfile.description: The band boundaries, as an age in days: younger than `high` is high, than `good` good, than `aging` aging; older is stale
